title: Symmetry protected quantum many body scars through half-gauging
authors: Weslei B. Fontana, Fabrizio G. Oliviero, Yi-Ping Huang
abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry defects insertion and the phenomena of quantum many body scarring. We exploit a class of models obtained from an embedding mechanism that defines a stochastic matrix form hamiltonian, hosting zero energy many body scarred states. Such models display an interesting playground to explore the consequences of dualities, half-gauging operations and so on. We first show that inside this class of models, what are the conditions to still have scared states after defect insertion. The main result of our work is a detailed analysis of half-gauging in such chains, which introduces a non-trivial interface in our system, leading to scarred states protected by the underlying symmetries. The conclusions for half-gauged scarred systems are general and may lead to fruitful directions for higher dimension scarred physics and their robustness.
summary: This paper analyzes how Quantum Many-Body Scars persist in structured quantum chains when subjected to symmetry defects or boundary conditions via half-gauging. The core finding is that the underlying symmetries dictate the survival and structure of these non-thermal states, leading to an enlarged, protected subspace. This provides general guidelines for engineering robust quantum phases in higher dimensions.
main_problem: The study investigates the persistence of Quantum Many-Body Scars (QMBS) states when symmetry defects or gauging operations are introduced into the system.
main_result: The analysis shows that the protected nature of the scars can be maintained, leading to an 'anomalous QMBS subspace' protected by the underlying symmetries, even after complex perturbations.
method: The authors employ techniques including defect insertion analysis, duality transformations, and the specialized 'half-gauging' procedure to probe the robustness of the scarred subspace.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a class of $\alpha$-chains, specifically $k$-chains, governed by a Hamiltonian $H^{(k)}_s$ derived from an embedding mechanism. The analysis compares scars protected by SPT anchors versus symmetry-breaking anchors.
key_observables: QMBS states (non-thermal eigenstates), protected degeneracies, and the structure of the symmetry algebra generated by the gauging procedure.
important_parameters: The chain length $k$, the defect strength $\beta$, and the gauging parameterization.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the half-gauging procedure successfully recovers a protected, structured subspace, and that the system's behavior can be characterized by its symmetry structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the entanglement entropy profile for the $k=2$ chain, illustrating the persistence of scarring under defect introduction.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the scarred model, then analyzing the effect of defect insertion distinguishing between SPT and symmetry-breaking anchors, and finally detailing the core result using half-gauging to reveal interface-protected degeneracies.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses the robustness of topologically or symmetry-protected quantum states against local perturbations (defects) and engineered boundaries (interfaces), which is central to understanding fault-tolerant quantum computation and exotic quantum phases.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Entanglement entropy profile in the correspond- ing sectors with Z2 defect insertion. (a) The profile cor- responding to the sector with a single defect at site j = 7 and (b) the sector with the insertion of two defects (sites, j = 7, 10) on each of the corresponding sub-lattices. In both situations, the scarring is preserved and we are able to identify the single QMBS state at zero-energy, as de- picted in the figure by the red circle. These were ob- tained from the exact diagonalization of the correspond- ing model over a periodic chain of size L = 14 sites. The other parameters of the model were fixed as β = 0.5 and α = 0.3.

FIG. 2: Entanglement entropy profile for the scarred 3- chain. (a) The profile corresponding to the sector with zero defects. (b) The profile corresponding to the sec- tor with a single defect at j = 7. Unlike the previous case, inserting a defect for this chain, completely destroy the scarring of the model, as predicted by our analytical analysis. These were obtained from exact diagonaliza- tion of the corresponding model for a periodic chain of size L = 14 sites. The other parameters of the model were fixed as β = 0.5 and α = 0.3.

FIG. 3: Entanglement profile of the 1-chain containing a single duality interface. Due to the anomaly, the QMBS subspace increases from a 2-fold degeneracy to a 4-fold degeneracy, which is now protected by the underlying symmetries. In the inset, we split the states in energy by hand, simply to make explicitly the presence of the four states. These were obtained by means of exact diagonal- ization of an open chain of L = 14 sites. The parameters were fixed as β = 0.5 and α = 0.3.

FIG. 4: Loschmidt echo of the scar states compared with a generic high-energy volume-law state. The strong re- vivals of |S±⟩originate from coherent oscillations within an almost isolated two-level subspace, while a random state in the full Hilbert space state (in green) rapidly loses memory of its initial condition. Exact diagonaliza- tion of a chain with L = 10, α = 0.3, β = 0.3, hz = 0.05.
